reason: In 'Sepals 5, ... obtuse, margin membranous' the margin belongs to the sepals. The annotation 'sepal margin' with texture 'membranous' matches.
'Leaves ... apex acute and mucronate': the leaf apex is acute.
'Cymes (1-)2-3(-13) flowered' gives the number of flowers per inflorescence. The usual range is 2-3, the extremes are 1 and 13, and the container is the inflorescence. All are right.

fix: In 'broadened at the base', the words 'at the base' are a position. Keep that position on the costa; do not drop it.
reason: The flora says only the base of the costa is sometimes much broadened. Without the position, the annotation says the whole costa is wider, which is false for a costa that tapers above.
'Stems usually erect, (3–)5–12(–15) dm' converts correctly: 50-120 cm with extremes 30 and 150 cm. Height fits erect shrub stems.
'pistillate ... stout, 21-60 × 8-16 mm' is the size of the female catkin. 8-16 mm is its width, and the 'female' context (PATO_0000383) is set.

target: pyrene (fruit stone: endocarp with its seed); nearest PO is endocarp PO_0009086
fix: The PO lexicon lists 'pyrene' as a synonym of seed (PO_0009010). In Boraginaceae/Ehretia and in drupes, a pyrene is the stone: the hard endocarp around one or more seeds. Do not ground 'pyrene' to seed.
reason: 'pyrenes segment-shaped, 4 mm long' measures the endocarp segments of the fruit, not the seed inside them.
'Ovules 4, shortly funiculate' means the ovules have a funicle. 'Funicle present' is true, although the word 'shortly' is not recorded.
'style linear, equaling stamens': the style's length equals the stamens' length (ratio 1).
'Each flower has 4 broad petals': the petal count is 4.
A scape is a leafless peduncle (flower stalk). 'Scapes ± equaling leaves' is its length compared with the leaves, and the 'approximately' qualifier is kept.
In a tuberous Begonia, 'Leaves solitary' means one leaf per plant, so a leaf count of 1 is right.
'Stamens shorter than petals': the stamens have decreased length compared with the petals.
'styles 5, free': the style count is 5.
'flowers in apical subumbels': the flowers are in umbel-like clusters, so an umbelliform inflorescence is a fair reading.
'Branches ... terete, slender': the branches are slender.
In 'bracteoles ... 1.5–5 × 0.3–0.8 mm', the first range (1.5-5 mm) is the length.

target: position: lower and middle cauline (stem) leaves
fix: When a statement starts with 'Lower and middle stem leaves', keep that position on the leaf bearer. Otherwise the measurement is wrongly applied to every leaf.
reason: Only the lower and middle stem leaves are 6-19 × 2-6 cm. The upper leaves are smaller, so 'leaf width 2-6 cm' for all leaves is false.
'bois jaune citron clair' (light lemon-yellow wood): the wood (secondary xylem) is yellow.

fix: 'X not seen', 'unknown' or 'not known' mean the part has not been observed. They do not mean the part is absent. Do not annotate these as 'absent'; drop the annotation.
reason: 'Capsules not seen' means nobody has seen the fruit. It does not mean the plant has no fruit.

fix: 'glaucous' means covered with a bluish-white waxy bloom. Ground it to PATO glaucous, not to 'green, approximately'.
reason: The flora says the leaf blades are glaucous. It does not say they are roughly green.
'Cyme ... 5-9-flowered': 5-9 flowers per inflorescence.
'minutely pubescent, at least when young' is said of the leaf blades, and the 'young' context (PATO_0000309) is set.
'surfaces glabrous or sparsely stellate-hairy' gives two alternatives for the hairiness of the leaf blade: glabrous or hairy (sparsely). The reading is right.
'filets ... insérés sur un androgynophore': the filaments are inserted on the androgynophore. The word 'généralement' (usually) is not recorded, but the core statement holds.

target: midlobe of the lip (no term found in PO or FLOPO; use lip with a 'middle lobe' position)
fix: In orchid lip descriptions, a measurement after 'midlobe' or 'lateral lobes' belongs to that lobe, not to the whole lip.
reason: The 1.2 cm length is that of the lip's midlobe. The context gives the whole lip as 2-2.4 cm wide, so the whole lip is larger.
'petiole 5-7 cm, not winged': the petiole is not winged, and the negation is right.
'bracts ovate-lanceolate, shorter than calyx': the bracts have decreased length compared with the calyx.
'not serrulate' in a perigynium description refers to its margins/edges. Annotating the perigynium as 'not serrulate' keeps the meaning.

fix: In a lamina description of the form 'X to Y, narrowly cuneate', the first tip-shape words (obtuse, acuminate) describe the apex and 'cuneate' describes the base. Ground them to leaf apex and leaf base.
reason: Obtuse and acuminate are shapes of the leaf tip, not of the whole lamina, which was already given as oblanceolate to narrowly elliptic.
